Package io.webagent4j.recording

Record Class WorkflowRecordingV2

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.webagent4j.recording.WorkflowRecordingV2
Record Components:
schemaVersion - the canonical JSON schema version this recording conforms to
recordingId - the non-sensitive caller-supplied recording identifier, persisted verbatim
capturedAt - the caller-supplied capture time
workflowId - the recorded execution's workflow identifier - always equal to plan.workflowId()
status - the recorded execution's overall terminal outcome
plan - the recorded execution's own structural plan, used to check compatibility with a live Workflow without inspecting its internals
nodes - the top-level recorded execution nodes, in execution order
failure - the overall recorded failure, present exactly when status is WorkflowStatus.FAILED
public record WorkflowRecordingV2(RecordingSchemaVersionV2 schemaVersion, RecordingId recordingId, Instant capturedAt, WorkflowId workflowId, WorkflowStatus status, WorkflowExecutionPlan plan, List<RecordedExecutionNodeV2> nodes, Optional<RecordedFailure> failure) extends Record
An immutable, versioned, tree-shaped recording of one workflow execution - the Recording V2 root type.

Unlike WorkflowRecording (Recording V1), which records a flat, already-selected step sequence, this type also carries the recorded execution's own WorkflowExecutionPlan - the same deterministic, backend-neutral structural description WorkflowPlanner.plan(io.webagent4j.workflow.Workflow) produces from a live Workflow definition, built without ever running it - and a RecordedExecutionNodeV2 tree that preserves which branch each CONDITIONAL step actually selected, mirroring WorkflowExecutionTree rather than the flat WorkflowResult alone. A consumer can check recording.plan().equals(WorkflowPlanner.plan(liveWorkflow)) to decide, without any separate input/output-list bookkeeping, whether a live workflow is structurally the same one this recording was captured from.

Like V1, a recording is data, not a program: it has no execute() method, retains no action factory, prepared action plan, page, or browser reference, and does not replay itself. This type intentionally has no relationship to WorkflowRecording beyond sharing this module's RecordedFailure, RecordedCondition, and RecordedAction projections and its versioning discipline: there is no implicit or automatic V1-to-V2 conversion anywhere in this module, and nothing here accepts or produces a WorkflowRecording. See docs/recording.md for the full architecture, the V1/V2 relationship, and the rationale for what is and is not recorded.

This type's own invariants validate nodes() on two independent axes, both enforced unconditionally by this compact constructor - so no construction path (direct Java construction, WorkflowRecorderV2, or JsonWorkflowRecordingV2Codec#decode) can ever produce an instance that skips either one. RecordingV2Invariants validates that nodes() could itself have resulted from one real, sequential, fail-fast execution - the same scope WorkflowRecording's invariants already have for V1's flat list - plus that plan() and workflowId() agree with each other. RecordingV2PlanTreeValidator additionally proves nodes() is itself a structurally authorized path through plan(): the same step IDs and types at the same positions, any recorded output matching its plan declaration exactly, and every recorded branch selection and its children corresponding exclusively to that plan node's matching branch - and bounds both structures' conditional-nesting depth. A hostile or corrupted recording can no longer pair a plan that matches a live workflow exactly with a fabricated or mismatched execution tree; Deterministic Replay's ReplayValidator relies on this as an already-guaranteed precondition and only has to additionally check plan() itself against the live Workflow's current structure.

recordingId and capturedAt are always caller-supplied, exactly like WorkflowId: neither is generated inside this module, so the same recording data always produces the same identity and timestamp regardless of how many times it is captured or re-encoded. Identifiers such as recordingId are persisted verbatim, are visible through record toString() output, and must contain only non-sensitive metadata.
